title: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
requirement: Would prohibit providing covered coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords and landlords’ use of those algorithms when setting residential rents or occupancy levels.
coverage_conditions: Applies to coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old to calculate and recommend rental terms for future leases in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and competitors.
exemptions: Excludes specified products or processes involving aggregated anonymous data, affordable-housing rent or income limits, market research for project financing, appraisals, and software-development research, testing, or training, subject to the conditions in the ordinance.
quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
conflict_note: Two published effective dates: March 1, 2026 in the ordinance text and January 2026 in an August 2026 law-firm alert. Both are before 2026-10-01, so the ban is in force either way; we use the later date.
interaction: Reviewed: Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S. was adopted by the Berkeley City Council, so it is enacted law, not a pending bill. The model read 'passed to print' as not yet passed.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. Prohibited actions include refusing to rent or terminating a tenancy based on criminal history, requiring disclosure or authorization to obtain criminal history, or treating applicants or tenants differently on that basis. The ordinance also requires written notice and an opportunity to respond before taking action based on criminal history.
coverage_conditions: Applies to current and prospective tenants in Berkeley.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; certain owner-occupied properties with 1–3 units; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; and units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add or replace roommates.
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

title: 2026 Adjustments of Relocation Assistance Payments
requirement: Owners must pay relocation assistance for owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions. Effective January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, with an additional $6,471 for qualifying households.
key_value: $19,413 standard; $6,471 additional for qualifying households
coverage_conditions: Applies to owner move-in evictions and evictions to remove a property from the rental housing market under the Ellis Act; the additional payment is for qualifying households.
quoted_span:
The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to
$19,413
.
The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to
$6,471

title: Tenant screening fee limits and accounting
requirement: The screening fee is capped at $68.96 for 2026. Landlords must provide a copy of a consumer credit report within 7 days of receipt, a receipt and itemized accounting of screening costs, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.
key_value: $68.96 maximum screening fee for 2026
coverage_conditions: Prospective tenants charged a tenant screening fee.
quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96
conflict_note: Two figures are published. Civil Code section 1950.6 states a $30 base, adjusted each year with the Consumer Price Index. Berkeley's Rent Board states the 2026 maximum is $68.96. The corpus has no single official statewide dollar amount for 2026.
interaction: Reviewed: The verified quote left out the dollar amount, which sits on the next line of the same page. The brief names this cap as an open question.

title: Reusable screening reports
requirement: If a tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
coverage_conditions: A tenant provides a reusable screening report.
quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

title: Restrictions on charging and retaining screening fees
requirement: A landlord cannot charge a screening fee when no rental unit is available. The landlord must return the fee to an applicant not selected, unless the landlord follows the stated application-order and no-charge-for-unconsidered-applicants policy.
coverage_conditions: Prospective rental applicants.
exemptions: The described alternative policy is to review applications in order received, rent to the first qualified applicant, and not charge applicants who are not considered.
quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected

title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees associated with existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
requirement: An owner or agent cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy, including fees associated with a roommate’s departure or a request to add or replace a roommate.
coverage_conditions: Existing tenants of residential rental property.
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part

title: Annual General Adjustment cap
requirement: The Annual General Adjustment (AGA) for fully covered rental units cannot exceed 5%. The cap does not prevent landlords from using banked AGAs to raise rent to the rent ceiling.
key_value: Maximum AGA: 5%
coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units.
citation: Measure BB Changes to Berkeley's Rent Ordinance | Berkeley Rent Board
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

title: Just cause required for covered units
requirement: A tenant in a fully or partially covered unit cannot be evicted unless there is just cause.
coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance.
citation: Measure BB Changes to Berkeley's Rent Ordinance | Berkeley Rent Board
quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause”

title: Minimum rental debt for nonpayment eviction
requirement: A landlord may evict for nonpayment only if the tenant owes rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent for an equivalent-size unit in the Oakland-Fremont metro area, using the HUD value for the fiscal year in which rent is demanded.
key_value: At least one month of applicable Fair Market Rent
coverage_conditions: The rule concerns eviction for nonpayment of rent; the document describes just-cause protections for fully or partially covered units.
citation: Measure BB Changes to Berkeley's Rent Ordinance | Berkeley Rent Board
quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR

title: Eviction for failure to sign a substantially similar lease prohibited
requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
coverage_conditions: The document describes just-cause protections for fully or partially covered units.
citation: Measure BB Changes to Berkeley's Rent Ordinance | Berkeley Rent Board
quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

title: Requirements for eviction based on material lease-term violations
requirement: A material lease term must be mutually agreed upon; the alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord; the landlord must demonstrate unreasonable tenant behavior; and the notice to stop the violation must adequately specify the term, violation, and resulting harm.
coverage_conditions: Evictions based on violations of a material lease term.
citation: Measure BB Changes to Berkeley's Rent Ordinance | Berkeley Rent Board
quoted_span:
Material lease terms only include mutually agreed upon lease terms.
The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord.
The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.

title: Eviction notice contents and filing requirements
requirement: A notice terminating a tenancy must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and provide its current housing counseling phone number and website address. The landlord must file copies of termination notices, notices to quit, and summons and complaints with the Rent Board no later than three business days after service.
key_value: File within three business days after service
citation: Measure BB Changes to Berkeley's Rent Ordinance | Berkeley Rent Board
quoted_span: Any notice terminating a tenancy must contain a statement that advice about the notice is available from the Rent Board, the current phone number for the Rent Board’s Housing counseling services, and the current address of the Rent Board’s website.

title: Security deposit amount limits
requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may charge no more than one month’s rent for furnished or unfurnished units. Landlords meeting the stated small-owner and ownership conditions may charge up to two months’ rent.
key_value: One month’s rent; up to two months’ rent for qualifying landlords
coverage_conditions: Applies to furnished and unfurnished units; the two-month limit applies to landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, with ownership held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC whose members are all natural persons.
exemptions: The stated qualifying small landlords may charge up to two months’ rent.
quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

title: Treatment of last month’s rent
requirement: Last month’s rent is considered part of the security deposit; first month’s rent is not.
quoted_span: Last month’s rent IS considered part of the security deposit

title: Photographs at the start of a tenancy
requirement: For a tenancy beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of the tenancy to document its condition.
coverage_conditions: Tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025.
quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

title: Move-out walk-through inspection
requirement: The landlord must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify items needing repair or cleaning.
key_value: During the last two weeks of the tenancy
quoted_span: Under state law, landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy to identify any items that need repair/cleaning.

title: Permitted security deposit deductions
requirement: A landlord may deduct only amounts reasonably necessary for rent default, tenant- or guest-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear, qualifying cleaning, and—if allowed by the lease—restoring or replacing personal property or furniture, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
coverage_conditions: Cleaning to return the unit to its starting level of cleanliness applies to tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003.
exemptions: Normal or ordinary wear and tear is excluded.
quoted_span: A landlord may deduct only the amount that is reasonably necessary to: Cover rent default Repair damages caused by a tenant or a tenant's guest other than normal wear and tear

title: Limits on professional cleaning deductions
requirement: A landlord may not require payment for, or claim against the tenant or deposit for, professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to its starting condition, minus ordinary wear and tear.
exemptions: Professional cleaning may be charged when reasonably necessary to return the premises to the condition at the start of the tenancy, minus ordinary wear and tear.
quoted_span: The landlord cannot require a tenant to pay for, or assert a claim against the tenant or the security deposit for professional carpet cleaning or other professional cleaning services

title: Return and accounting of security deposits
requirement: The landlord must return the deposit or remaining portion within 21 days after the tenant leaves the unit vacant. If deductions are made, the landlord must provide a written itemized statement and supporting documents for repair or cleaning charges; starting January 1, 2025, the landlord must also provide proof that necessary repairs were completed.
key_value: 21 days
quoted_span: All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned within 21 days after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

title: Photographs before security-deposit deductions for repairs or cleaning
requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit after regaining possession but before repairs or cleaning for which a deposit deduction is intended. The photographs and a written explanation of the cost must be provided to the tenant with the itemized statement.
coverage_conditions: Applies when the landlord intends to deduct for repairs or cleaning.
quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.

title: Security deposit interest
requirement: Landlords must pay interest on security deposits at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
key_value: Annual interest, with a prorated amount when the tenant moves out before year-end
coverage_conditions: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley’s Rent Ordinance.
exemptions: Units not covered by Berkeley’s Rent Ordinance are not identified as covered by this requirement on the source page.
quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year

title: 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA)
requirement: Eligible landlords may increase 2025 permanent rent ceilings by the 2026 AGA, subject to the conditions and tenant notice requirements in Regulation 1148.
coverage_conditions: Applies to eligible landlords and 2025 permanent rent ceilings; Regulation 1148 sets qualifying conditions and required tenant notice.
exemptions: May not adjust rents for tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025, and whose rents were set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
citation: Rent Board Regulation 1148; Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.76.110A
quoted_span: adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026.

title: Guide to Coverage under Berkeley’s Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
requirement: The guide indicates that rent control applies to fully covered units and does not apply to partially covered or exempt units. It does not state a rent-increase limit or formula.
key_value: Rent Control: Yes for fully covered units; No for partially covered and exempt units
coverage_conditions: Fully covered examples include most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, qualifying single-family tenancies that began before 1996, and rooming houses meeting the stated conditions.
exemptions: Partially covered examples include new construction built and receiving a Certificate of Occupancy after June 1980, qualifying later-starting single-family tenancies, and most condominiums. The table lists Golden Duplexes and other specified unit types as exempt.
citation: Guide to Coverage under Berkeley’s Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

title: Guide to Coverage under Berkeley’s Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Just Cause Ordinance
requirement: The table indicates that just-cause-for-eviction coverage applies to fully and partially covered units, and does not apply to units listed as exempt.
key_value: Yes for fully and partially covered units; No for exempt units
coverage_conditions: Fully covered examples include most units in multifamily properties built before 1980. Partially covered examples include qualifying new construction, most condominiums, and listed units with specified government subsidies.

requirement: The table indicates that security deposit interest applies to fully and partially covered units, and not to units listed as exempt.
key_value: Security Deposit Interest: Yes for fully and partially covered units; No for exempt units

exemptions: The table lists Golden Duplexes, certain owner-shared kitchen or bath arrangements, specified ADU tenancies, university rental units, and nonprofit cooperatives as exempt.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
requirement: Covered housing providers may not impose a blanket policy denying housing to people with arrests or convictions and must consider applicants case by case. They must not consider arrests that did not result in conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions more than five years old.
key_value: Convictions more than 5 years old are not considered.
coverage_conditions: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
exemptions: The policy’s tenant-selection rule does not apply where there is a direct relationship between the conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others; it does not apply to current criminal behavior. Conflicting federal or state law preempts the policy.
citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
quoted_span: will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis.

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
requirement: Covered agents may not use an applicant’s credit score to approve or deny a housing application. Credit history may be considered only in lieu of rental history to assess ability to pay when rental history is unavailable.
coverage_conditions: Agents covered by the policy: housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
exemptions: Credit history may be considered when rental history is unavailable, but only to determine ability to pay rent.
citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
quoted_span: The agent agrees not to use the applicant credit score to approve or deny housing applications.

title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
requirement: The bill proposed authorizing Boston to implement rent stabilization; it does not specify a rent-increase limit.
quoted_span: the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization

title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
requirement: The bill proposed authorizing Boston to implement tenant eviction protections; it does not specify the protections or conditions.
quoted_span: the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections

title: Security-deposit discrimination based on familial status
requirement: Housing providers may not charge households with children a higher security deposit as a discriminatory condition or rule.
coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers and rules that discriminate against households with children.
quoted_span: Prohibiting housing providers from having conditions or rules that discriminate against households with children, such as charging a higher security deposit to households with children

title: Fair-housing limits on tenant screening
requirement: Tenant screening, including screening conducted by a third party, may not discriminate based on a protected characteristic.
coverage_conditions: Applies to prospective-tenant screening by housing providers and third-party tenant screening companies when discrimination is based on a protected characteristic.
quoted_span: Screening prospective tenants – including when done by a third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic

title: Source-of-income discrimination in rental housing
requirement: Housing providers may not discriminate against applicants or tenants based on their source of income, including by applying different tenancy terms or charging a higher security deposit because of that source.
coverage_conditions: Applies to applicants and renters; examples include public assistance, rental assistance, housing subsidies, and wages.
quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).

title: Limits on considering criminal history in rental decisions
requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile-system matters, and may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal history. A conviction used to deny an application must be directly related to the applicant’s ability to be a good tenant and not threaten health, safety, or property; consider the crime’s nature and severity and time elapsed.
coverage_conditions: Applies when a housing provider considers an applicant’s criminal history or intends to deny an application based on a criminal conviction.
quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.

title: Cartwright Act: common pricing algorithms
requirement: Prohibits using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce, and prohibits using or distributing one to coerce another person to set or adopt its recommended price or commercial term.
coverage_conditions: Applies to common pricing algorithms using competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. The prohibition covers products or services in California.
exemptions: The definition of “Person” does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
quoted_span: (b) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state.
interaction: Effective date from Cal. Const. art. IV, sec. 8(c): statutes chaptered without an urgency clause take effect January 1 of the next year.

title: Just cause termination of tenancy
requirement: After the applicable occupancy period, an owner may not terminate a covered residential tenancy without just cause, which must be stated in the written termination notice. Just cause includes specified at-fault and no-fault grounds. For curable lease violations, the owner must first provide notice and an opportunity to cure. A no-fault termination also requires relocation assistance or a rent waiver.
key_value: 12 months of continuous, lawful occupancy; where additional adult tenants are added before an existing tenant has occupied for 24 months, the statutory 12-month or 24-month conditions apply.
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property after the occupancy threshold in subdivision (a), subject to the statutory exemptions.
exemptions: Subdivision (e) exempts, among others, transient and tourist hotel occupancy; specified institutional and care housing; dormitories; units where the tenant shares kitchen or bathroom facilities with an owner who lives there; certain owner-occupied residences and properties; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); and certain separately alienable residential properties if specified ownership and notice conditions are met.
quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

title: California Civil Code § 1946.2 — Just cause for termination of tenancy
requirement: After all tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more, or at least one tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied it for 24 months or more, the landlord must provide a statement of cause in a notice to terminate the tenancy.
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property subject to this section. Local just-cause ordinances apply instead where the statute specifies, including ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and qualifying more-protective ordinances adopted or amended after that date.
exemptions: The excerpt identifies exceptions for certain properties subject to local just-cause ordinances, certain affordable housing, and homeowners of mobilehomes; other exemptions may be specified in portions of the section not included in the document.
quoted_span: after all of the tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months or more or at least one of the tenants has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 24 months or more, a landlord must provide a statement of cause in any notice to terminate a tenancy.

title: California statewide rent increase limit
requirement: For covered residential rental units, an owner may not increase the gross rental rate over a 12-month period by more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, calculated from the lowest gross rental rate charged during the preceding 12 months. If the same tenant remains, increases may occur in no more than two increments during that period.
key_value: 5% plus CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower
coverage_conditions: Applies to rent increases subject to subdivision (a); the initial rental rate for a new tenancy with no tenant from the prior tenancy remaining in lawful possession is not subject to the cap. Local rent controls may impose a lower limit.
exemptions: Includes specified affordable housing; dormitories owned and operated by educational institutions; housing subject to qualifying lower local rent controls; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, except mobilehomes; qualifying separately alienable properties where the owner meets the statutory criteria and gives the required notice; and qualifying owner-occupied properties containing two dwelling units. Does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome.
quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower

title: Residential security amount limits
requirement: For residential property used as the tenant’s dwelling, a landlord generally may not demand or receive security exceeding one month’s rent, in addition to first-month rent. A qualifying small landlord may demand up to two months’ rent, subject to the service-member limitation. An advance payment of at least six months’ rent is permitted when the lease term is six months or longer.
key_value: Generally one month’s rent; up to two months for qualifying landlords; advance rent of at least six months is permitted for qualifying lease terms.
coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant’s dwelling.
exemptions: The one-month limit does not prohibit an advance payment of at least six months’ rent when the lease term is six months or longer. The two-month limit exception applies only if the landlord is a natural person or qualifying LLC and owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units offered for rent; it does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. The subdivision does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.
quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent

title: Higher security charged to a service member
requirement: If a landlord or agent charges a service member higher-than-standard or higher-than-advertised security because of credit history, credit score, housing history, or another tenant-related factor, the landlord must provide a written statement of the amount and reason by the lease-signing date. The additional security must be returned after no more than six months of residency if the tenant is not in arrears for rent during that period, and the lease must state the return date.
key_value: Return the additional security after no more than six months of residency if rent is not in arrears during that period.
coverage_conditions: A service member renting residential property in which the service member will reside, where higher security is charged due to a tenant-related factor.
quoted_span: On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security

title: Permitted security-deposit deductions
requirement: A landlord may claim from security only amounts reasonably necessary for the purposes specified in subdivision (b). The landlord may not charge for preexisting damage or defective conditions, ordinary wear and tear, or professional cleaning unless reasonably necessary to return the premises to their inception-of-tenancy condition, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
coverage_conditions: Claims against a residential tenant or the tenant’s security.
exemptions: Reasonable costs to restore the premises to their inception-of-tenancy condition, excluding ordinary wear and tear, may be claimed as provided by the section.
quoted_span: the landlord may claim of the security only those amounts as are reasonably necessary for the purposes specified in subdivision (b).

title: Tenant-requested initial inspection before move-out
requirement: After notice of an intention to terminate the tenancy or before the lease ends, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection and the right to attend. If requested, the landlord must conduct the inspection at a reasonable time no earlier than two weeks before termination or lease end, and provide an itemized statement of proposed repair or cleaning deductions.
key_value: At least 48 hours’ prior written notice of the inspection date and time, unless both parties sign a written waiver.
coverage_conditions: An initial inspection is requested by the tenant.
exemptions: The requirements do not apply when the tenancy is terminated pursuant to subdivisions (2), (3), or (4) of Code of Civil Procedure Section 1161.
quoted_span: the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.

title: Move-in photographs
requirement: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must take photographs of the unit immediately before or at the inception of the tenancy.
coverage_conditions: Tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit immediately before, or at the inception of, the tenancy.

title: Photographs before and after deposit-deductible repairs or cleaning
requirement: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit within a reasonable time after possession is returned and before repairs or cleaning for which a security deduction or claim will be made, and again within a reasonable time after those repairs or cleaning are completed.
coverage_conditions: Repairs or cleaning for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit.
quoted_span: Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings

title: Return and accounting of security
requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must provide an itemized statement of the basis for and amount of security received and its disposition, and return any remaining security, subject to the section’s timing and return-method provisions.
key_value: 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises.
coverage_conditions: Residential security held by the landlord when the tenancy ends.
quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises

title: Landlord holds security for tenant
requirement: Security must be held by the landlord for the tenant who is party to the lease or agreement, and the tenant’s claim to the security takes priority over claims of the landlord’s creditors.
coverage_conditions: Security held under a residential rental agreement.
quoted_span: The claim of a tenant to the security shall be prior to the claim of any creditor of the landlord.

title: Documentation of security-deposit deductions
requirement: When deducting for repairs or cleaning, a landlord generally must provide supporting documentation with the itemized statement. If the work is done by the landlord or an employee, the statement must describe the work, time spent, and reasonable hourly rate. For work performed by others, the landlord must provide the bill, invoice, or receipt and, when needed, the provider’s contact information. Material costs and applicable photographs and cost explanations must also be provided. A good-faith estimate may be used in specified circumstances, with follow-up documentation due within 14 calendar days after the repair is completed or documentation is received.
key_value: 14 calendar days; documentation exception for deductions totaling no more than $125
coverage_conditions: Applies to deductions from residential security for repairs or cleaning.
exemptions: The landlord need not initially provide the specified repair-and-cleaning documentation if those deductions together do not exceed $125 or the tenant has signed a qualifying waiver. If the tenant requests documentation within 14 calendar days after receiving the itemized statement, the landlord must provide it within 14 calendar days after receiving the request.
quoted_span: The landlord shall also include, along with and at the same time the itemized statement is sent, copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises

title: Disposition of security when landlord’s interest ends
requirement: When a landlord’s interest in the premises terminates, the landlord or agent must within a reasonable time either transfer the remaining security, after lawful deductions, to the successor in interest and notify the tenant of the transfer and relevant details, or return the remaining security to the tenant with an accounting. Before a voluntary transfer, the landlord must provide the successor a written statement of the remaining security, deductions, and election.
key_value: Within a reasonable time
coverage_conditions: Applies upon termination or voluntary transfer of a landlord’s interest in the premises.

title: Bad-faith security claims and nonrefundable deposits
requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not characterize security as nonrefundable. Bad-faith claiming or retaining security in violation of the section, or bad-faith demand for replacement security in violation of the section, may result in statutory damages of up to twice the security amount in addition to actual damages.
key_value: Statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security, plus actual damages
coverage_conditions: Applies to security deposits and rental agreements covered by the section.
quoted_span: A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

title: Application screening fee amount limit
requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee only up to the actual out-of-pocket costs and reasonable value of time spent obtaining applicant information, and the fee may not exceed $30 per applicant, subject to annual CPI adjustment.
key_value: Maximum $30 per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index.
coverage_conditions: Applies when a landlord or agent receives a request to rent residential property and charges an application screening fee.

title: Conditions for charging application screening fees
requirement: A landlord may not charge an application screening fee when they know or should know that no rental unit is available now or within a reasonable time. A fee may be charged only when the landlord offers a qualifying screening process: completed applications considered in received order under written criteria, with the first applicant meeting those criteria approved and fees charged only when an application is considered; or the entire fee is returned to applicants not selected within the specified deadline. The landlord must provide an itemized receipt and return any unused portion of the fee when specified screening services are not performed.
coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords or agents charging an application screening fee to an applicant for residential rental property.
quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

title: Aggregate income standards for rental housing
requirement: A housing provider may not use a financial or income standard that fails to count the aggregate income of people residing or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married people living together.
coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing.
quoted_span: To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income of married persons residing together or proposing to reside together.

title: Income standards for applicants with government rent subsidies
requirement: When there is a government rent subsidy, eligibility financial or income standards must be based on the portion of rent the tenant will pay, rather than the full rent.
coverage_conditions: Applies when there is a government rent subsidy.
quoted_span: Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

title: Credit-history screening for applicants with government rent subsidies
requirement: When there is a government rent subsidy, a housing provider using an applicant’s credit history must offer the applicant the option to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay their portion of the rent. The provider must allow reasonable response time and reasonably consider that evidence instead of the credit history.
coverage_conditions: Applies when there is a government rent subsidy and the provider uses the applicant’s credit history in the rental application process.
exemptions: The provision does not limit the provider’s ability to request employment verification, landlord references, or identity verification.
quoted_span: Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant

title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance — tenant selection standards
requirement: Landlords, sellers, and rental agents may use reasonable applicant-selection standards only if applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Tenant selection may be based on an applicant’s ability to pay rent, care for the apartment, and respect others’ rights. Housing discrimination based on protected categories, including source of income, is prohibited.
coverage_conditions: Applies to real estate transactions including renting an apartment and the terms and conditions of tenancy.
exemptions: The source states an exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

title: Rent Control Exemption for 1-4 Unit Properties
requirement: Properties with 1-4 units are exempt from rent control.
exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties.

title: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
requirement: A landlord may terminate a covered tenancy only for a just cause reason. The listed reasons include specified tenant-fault causes and no-fault causes; relocation assistance may be required for no-fault evictions.
coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO; the tenant must have lived in the unit for at least six months or the original lease must have expired, whichever comes first.
exemptions: The source lists exceptions including transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, an owner's roommate, certain cooperatives and nonprofit facilities, and some HACLA- or government-owned properties.
citation: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) – LAHD
quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

title: Nonpayment-of-rent eviction threshold for RSO and JCO units
requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant for falling behind on rent unless the amount owed is higher than the applicable Fair Market Rent (FMR), which depends on the unit's bedroom size.
key_value: Amount owed must be higher than the applicable FMR
coverage_conditions: All RSO and JCO rental units.
citation: Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO) – LAHD
quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

title: RSO rent-increase frequency and allowable percentage
requirement: For rental units subject to the RSO, rent may be increased once every 12 months, by the allowable rent-increase percentage.
key_value: Once every 12 months; allowable percentage not stated in the document
coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO). The document says the RSO generally applies to covered rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, and certain replacement units.
quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

title: Additional-tenant rent increase
requirement: A landlord may increase rent by 10% for an additional tenant who is not a dependent and moves into the rental unit. The increase must be made within 60 days of the landlord learning about the additional tenant.
key_value: 10%; within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant
coverage_conditions: An additional tenant (not a dependent) moves into a rental unit subject to the RSO.
exemptions: The 10% increase is not permitted for an additional dependent.

title: No additional increase for an additional dependent
requirement: Landlords may no longer add a 10% rent increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy.

coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the RSO.

coverage_conditions: Rental units subject to the RSO.

requirement: Rent may be increased to the market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out or is evicted for one of the listed reasons, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement.
key_value: Market rate

Tenant is at-fault

title: RSO Rent Increase Calculator – LAHD

key_value: 30 days' written advance notice for rent increases of less than 10%

title: RSO Rent Increase Calculator – LAHD
requirement: Landlords may pass through the RSO and SCEP surcharges with proper written notice; the surcharges may be collected only after the landlord registers the units and gives written notice to the tenant.

title: Relocation assistance and filing requirements for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
requirement: For covered RSO or JCO units, landlords must pay relocation assistance and file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before evicting tenants in a no-fault eviction. A termination notice may be served only after filing the declaration, and a copy of the notice must be filed with LAHD within 3 days after service.
coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO); applies to tenant not-at-fault evictions.
exemptions: The bulletin lists exemptions from relocation assistance, including certain resident-manager replacement evictions and qualifying hazardous conditions caused by a natural disaster not resulting from landlord negligence.
quoted_span: All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO).

title: Demolition for new construction under the Resident Protections Ordinance
requirement: A landlord terminating a tenancy to demolish a Protected Unit for new construction must file the applicable eviction or withdrawal notice with LAHD, serve tenants written notice and file a copy within 3 business days, and pay relocation assistance under state or city law, whichever is higher. City relocation amounts must be enhanced for lower-income tenants when required by the RPO or HCA.
key_value: Relocation assistance is due within 15 days of serving the notice to terminate tenancy; the applicable amount is the higher amount required by state or city law.

title: General prohibition on rent control
requirement: Cities and towns may not enact, maintain, or enforce rent control, except a city or town that accepts Chapter 40P may adopt rent control subject to the stated conditions, including voluntary and uncoerced owner compliance after six months, limits on what the regulation may cover, and municipal compensation to affected owners.
coverage_conditions: Applies to cities and towns in Massachusetts.
exemptions: A city or town that accepts Chapter 40P may adopt rent control meeting the conditions in subsections (a)–(c). The regulation may not apply to a rental unit owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units or to a unit with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:

title: Protection against discrimination based on public assistance or housing subsidies
requirement: A person furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against an individual because the individual receives public assistance or a housing subsidy, including rental assistance or rental supplements.
coverage_conditions: Applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations.
quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient

title: Protection against housing discrimination because a person has children
requirement: Covered housing providers may not refuse to rent or lease housing, or discriminate in its terms, conditions, privileges, facilities, or services, because a person has children who occupy or will occupy the premises.
coverage_conditions: Applies to publicly assisted or multiple dwelling or contiguously located housing accommodations and other covered housing accommodations.
exemptions: Does not apply to specified dwellings of three apartments or fewer where an elderly or infirm person occupies one apartment and children would be a hardship; qualifying temporary leasing or subleasing of a residence ordinarily occupied by the owner or sublessor; or leasing one unit in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit.
quoted_span: to refuse to rent or lease or sell or otherwise to deny to or withhold from any person such accommodations because such person has a child or children who shall occupy the premises with such person or to discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of such accommodations

title: Determination of lease for nonpayment of rent
requirement: For nonpayment of rent due under a written lease, a landlord may determine the lease by giving the tenant 14 days’ written notice to quit. The tenant may prevent termination by paying or tendering all rent due, with interest and costs, by the specified deadline in a possession action. Special continuance and notice procedures apply when nonpayment was caused by a government payment delay.
key_value: 14 days
coverage_conditions: Nonpayment of rent due under a written lease.
citation: General Law - Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 11
quoted_span: fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease

title: Notice to determine estate at will
requirement: Either party may terminate an estate at will by written notice of three months, or, when rent is payable at intervals shorter than three months, by notice equal to the payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. For nonpayment, a landlord may give 14 days’ written notice to quit. If the tenant has not received a similar notice in the preceding 12 months, the tenant may prevent termination by paying or tendering all rent due within 10 days after receipt; the notice must inform the tenant of this right.
key_value: Three months; or the rent-payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. For nonpayment: 14 days’ notice and, where applicable, a 10-day cure period.
coverage_conditions: Applies to estates at will; the cure right applies to a tenant who has not received a similar nonpayment notice from the landlord within the preceding 12 months.
citation: General Law - Part II, Title I, Chapter 186, Section 12
quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party;

title: Security deposits
requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or the lessor’s agent may require a security deposit no greater than the first month’s rent. The deposit remains the tenant’s property and must be held in a separate, interest-bearing account. The statute also sets requirements for receipts, interest, return of the deposit, and permitted deductions.
key_value: Maximum security deposit: one month’s rent.
coverage_conditions: Residential real property; deposit required at or before commencement of a tenancy.
quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)

title: Transfer of security deposit to successor in interest
requirement: When the lessor transfers an interest in the property, the security deposit and accrued interest must be transferred to the successor in interest. The successor must notify the tenant in writing within 45 days, including the specified contact information, and is liable for retaining and returning the deposit under the section. If the deposit is not transferred, the successor generally assumes liability; for an occupying tenant, the successor may satisfy the obligation by providing equivalent free use and occupancy.
key_value: Written notice within 45 days
coverage_conditions: Applies when the lessor transfers an interest in the premises; granting a mortgage is not a transfer of interest.
exemptions: The stated successor-liability provision does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter 60, or to a qualifying foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession. A successor may satisfy the deposit obligation for a tenant still occupying the unit through equivalent free use and occupancy.
quoted_span: The successor in interest shall, within forty-five days from the date of said transfer, notify the tenant who made such security deposit that such security deposit was transferred to him and that he is holding said security deposit.

title: Forfeiture and damages for security-deposit violations
requirement: A lessor forfeits the right to retain any part of the security deposit for specified violations, including failure to hold the funds as required, transfer the deposit as required, or return the amount due within 30 days after tenancy ends. For failures to comply with the specified deposit-account, transfer, or return requirements, the tenant is entitled to three times the deposit or balance due, 5% interest from when payment became due, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees.
key_value: Return within 30 days; damages of three times the amount due plus 5% interest
coverage_conditions: The triple-damages provision applies to failures listed in subsection (6)(a), (d), or (e).
exemptions: A lease for a vacation or recreational purpose lasting 100 days or less is excluded from the section.
quoted_span: If the lessor or his agent fails to comply with clauses (a), (d), or (e) of subsection 6, the tenant shall be awarded damages in an amount equal to three times the amount of such security deposit or balance thereof to which the tenant is entitled plus interest at the rate of five per cent

title: Transfer of last-month rental advance
requirement: When a lessor transfers an interest in a dwelling unit after receiving rent in advance for the last month of tenancy, the lessor must credit the advance and accrued interest to the successor. The successor is liable for crediting the tenant and paying accrued interest, and must provide written notice within 45 days containing the specified information.
key_value: Written notice within 45 days
coverage_conditions: Applies when a lessor who received rent in advance for the last month transfers an interest in the dwelling unit; granting a mortgage is not a transfer of interest.
exemptions: The stated successor-liability provision does not apply to a city or town acquiring title under chapter 60, or to a qualifying foreclosing mortgagee or mortgagee in possession. A successor may satisfy the obligation for an occupying tenant through free use and occupancy for the period covered by the advance.
quoted_span: the lessor shall credit an amount equal to such rental advance together with any interest which has accrued thereon for the benefit of the tenant who made such rental advance, to the successor in interest of such lessor

title: Reprisal for reporting violations of law or for tenant's union activity
requirement: A notice of termination of tenancy (other than for nonpayment of rent) within six months after a tenant engages in specified protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal. The presumption may be rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence that the action was not retaliatory and had sufficient independent justification.
coverage_conditions: The tenant must have engaged in an activity listed in the statute, such as reporting a residential-premises violation or organizing or joining a tenants' union. The presumption applies to a notice issued within six months after the activity.
exemptions: The presumption does not apply to a notice of termination for nonpayment of rent.
quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
requirement: A housing provider may not make oral or written inquiries about an applicant’s criminal record before making a conditional offer, subject to the statutory exceptions for certain drug-related activity in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex-offender registration.
coverage_conditions: Applicants for rental dwelling units covered by the Act.
exemptions: The pre-offer inquiry restriction has exceptions for whether the applicant has been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for manufacturing or producing methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises, and whether the applicant is subject to lifetime registration under a State sex-offender registration program. A rental dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units is excluded from the Act’s definition of rental dwelling unit.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
requirement: A housing provider may not evaluate an applicant using specified records, including arrests or charges without conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, legally nullified convictions, juvenile adjudications, or sealed records. After a conditional offer, only specified convictions may be considered, subject to the statutory time limits; withdrawing an offer based on a criminal record requires a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest and an individualized assessment.
key_value: Permitted lookback periods include six years for specified first-degree indictable offenses, four years for specified second- or third-degree indictable offenses, and one year for specified fourth-degree indictable offenses; certain listed convictions are treated separately.
coverage_conditions: Applies to a housing provider’s evaluation of an applicant for a covered rental dwelling unit.
exemptions: The Act permits consideration of the specified convictions and records described in subsection b. of C.46:8-56 after a conditional offer.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not, either before or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on any of the following types of criminal records:

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing whether its eligibility criteria include review and consideration of criminal history, and inform the applicant that they may provide evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation, or other mitigating factors.
coverage_conditions: Applies before a housing provider accepts an application fee.

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
requirement: A housing provider may not knowingly or purposefully publish a housing advertisement stating that it will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except for the statutory exceptions. The Act also restricts discriminatory statements, inquiries, and use or dissemination of an applicant’s criminal record.
coverage_conditions: Housing advertisements and rental application or inquiry practices covered by the Act.
exemptions: The advertisement prohibition includes exceptions for specified drug-related criminal activity involving manufacture or production of methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime registration under a State sex-offender registration program.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses

title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test or request consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
coverage_conditions: Applicants to a housing provider for a covered rental dwelling unit.
quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.

title: Rental application fee remedy
requirement: After finding that a housing provider violated the act, the director may require the provider to return the applicant’s rental application fee, unless housing is provided to the applicant under paragraph (2).
coverage_conditions: Applies when the director finds a housing provider violated a provision of the act; the fee-return remedy does not apply if housing is provided under paragraph (2).
quoted_span: Unless housing is provided to the applicant pursuant to paragraph (2) of this subsection, the director may require that the applicant’s rental application fee be returned;

title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
requirement: A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee exceeding $50 to apply to lease or sublease residential rental property for dwelling purposes. The limit is subject to annual CPI adjustment beginning January 1, 2027.
key_value: $50 maximum, subject to annual CPI adjustment
coverage_conditions: Application or similar fees to lease or sublease residential rental property for dwelling purposes.
exemptions: Does not apply to a dwelling unit in a one-family or two-family dwelling offered for rent, or to a New Jersey Real Estate Commission licensee unless the licensee is the landlord.
quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

title: Eviction solely because the lease term ended
requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant solely because the lease term has ended.
quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant just because the lease term has ended.

title: Security deposit return after domestic-violence lease termination
requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the security deposit and interest available within 15 business days after termination. The landlord must notify the tenant in writing within three business days of when and where to collect it, and keep it available for 30 days. Any deductions must be itemized.
key_value: Make available within 15 business days; written notice within 3 business days; available for 30 days
coverage_conditions: A tenant terminates the lease under the Safe Housing Act due to domestic violence.
exemptions: Transient or seasonal rentals.
quoted_span: Within 15 business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent.

title: Maximum security deposit
requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit exceeding one and one-half times one month’s rent. A pet security deposit counts toward that combined limit.
key_value: 1.5 times one month’s rent
coverage_conditions: Applies to security deposits for covered residential rentals.

title: Annual security deposit increase limit
requirement: Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

quoted_span: Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: Security Deposit Law coverage
requirement: The Security Deposit Law applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. An owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling is excepted, but a tenant there may make the law applicable 30 days after sending the landlord a written request to comply.
key_value: 30 days after written request
coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant invokes the law by written request and waits 30 days.
quoted_span: The Security Deposit Law applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.

title: Handling and investment of security deposits
requirement: Security deposit money must be held in trust and may not be commingled with the landlord’s personal property or become the landlord’s asset. Deposits for ten or fewer units must be placed in an insured, interest-bearing account at a New Jersey bank or savings and loan association. coverage_conditions: The described account requirements distinguish between deposits for ten or fewer units and deposits for ten or more units.
exemptions: The account-investment provision does not apply to seasonal use or rental, as defined in the document.

title: Payment of security deposit interest
requirement: Interest or earnings on the security deposit belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited toward rent on the lease renewal or anniversary, or on January 31 if the tenant received written notice that payment will be made annually on that date.
quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing

title: Return of security deposit after tenancy
requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest earned, less lawful deductions. Any deductions require an itemized list sent to the tenant by registered or certified mail within that 30-day period.
key_value: 30 days after termination of tenancy
coverage_conditions: Applies after termination of a tenancy; the document describes a different termination date for a tenant who breaks a lease and moves out without legal cause.

title: Return of deposit after displacement
requirement: Within five business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit if an authorized public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified that displacement is expected to last longer than seven days. The landlord must tell the tenant within three business days after receiving notice where the deposit can be collected.

title: Rent increases and local rent control
requirement: New Jersey has no statewide rent-control limit. A landlord cannot increase rent during a lease term; to impose an increase after the lease ends, the landlord must give proper written notice and the increase must not be unconscionable or violate applicable municipal rent-control ordinances.
key_value: No fixed statewide cap; increases must not be unconscionable and must comply with applicable municipal ordinances.
coverage_conditions: Residential rental tenancies in New Jersey; local rent-control ordinances may govern where adopted.
exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent-control ordinances for 30 years after completion. Government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.
quoted_span: A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term. The old lease must be terminated, and the new lease must have the increased rental payment.

title: Credit reports and rental application fees

title: Protection from housing discrimination based on lawful source of income

title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
requirement: Prohibits rental property owners from receiving or using a coordinator’s services for consideration, coordinators from facilitating agreements that restrict competition, persons from engaging in parallel pricing coordination, and any person from performing a coordinating function.
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential dwelling units in New Jersey. exemptions: The act excludes specified research, statistical analysis, or testing not used to set or recommend terms for current or future leases; free public rent estimates; specified real estate brokerage databases; and government affordability controls. title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
requirement: Would prohibit a person from selling, licensing, or otherwise providing an algorithmic device to a landlord, and prohibit a landlord from using one to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
coverage_conditions: Applies to algorithmic devices that use or incorporate algorithms to calculate nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in San Diego.
exemptions: Excludes software that publishes reports using aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old or publicly available information, without recommending future rental rates or occupancy levels; also excludes software used to establish rates or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
quoted_span: It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.

title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
requirement: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property. It is also unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an algorithmic device to a landlord.
coverage_conditions: Applies to an algorithmic device that uses or incorporates algorithms to calculate nonpublic competitor data concerning rental rates, occupancy levels, or other residential leasing information to advise or recommend rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property in the City of San Diego.
exemptions: Excludes software or products used to publish reports based on aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data more than 90 days old, or publicly available information, when they do not recommend future rental rates or occupancy levels; also excludes software or products used to establish rental rates or income limits under affordable housing program guidelines.
quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

requirement: Residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. requirement: After 30 days, an owner may not terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice. Just cause includes specified at-fault and no-fault causes. coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies covered by the ordinance; the source states that the owner must state just cause in a written notice.
